result.title: Are Self-Evolving Agents Continual Learners?
result.summary: Large language model agents are often deployed in environments where new knowledge, tools, and workflows keep arriving. Such an agent is therefore expected to adapt continually, learning new tasks as they arrive without forgetting earlier ones. This resembles the continual learning problem, but at a pace that conventional gradient updates cannot sustain. Nonparametric self-evolving agents are a natural alternative: they adapt by rewriting their own harness, such as prompts, memory, and skills, from task feedback while the model weights stay frozen. We study whether such agents are effective continual learners across four drifting task streams that shift in topic, workflow, or domain (built from BIRD, BFCL, and ScienceWorld). Evaluating three representative methods spanning experience retrieval and self-modification (ReasoningBank, GEPA, and Meta-Harness), we find that although self-evolution improves aggregate performance on most streams, higher plasticity consistently comes at the cost of stability. Specifically, self-modifying methods apply global edits to a shared prompt or workspace, interfering with unseen tasks and overwriting earlier knowledge as the stream shifts. Conversely, similarity-based memory retrieval localizes updates across distant domains, but still retrieves foreign memories on unseen tasks and suffers from retrieval collision when similar queries require conflicting workflows. These findings show that current self-evolving agents remain incomplete continual learners.

AI.brief_summary: 研究非参数自进化 LLM agent 是否算有效的持续学习者：在四个主题/流程/领域漂移的任务流上评测 ReasoningBank、GEPA、Meta-Harness 三类方法，发现自进化虽提升总体表现，但可塑性提升总以稳定性下降为代价，自改写会覆盖旧知识，相似记忆检索在冲突流程下发生检索碰撞。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文不含视觉成分，但其关于共享提示/工作区的全局改写、记忆检索定位与冲突的机制分析，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态与视觉证据的局部更新、检索冲突处理提供可供核查的方法线索。
